cases.sentence: Не доходя одного дома до площади, он остановился у ворот, вынул из кармашка свистульку и свистнул изо всей силы, как бы подавая ___.
cases.explain: «условный знак» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The Schoolboy But Kolya did not hear her. At last he could go out. As he went out at the gate he looked round him, shrugged up his shoulders, and saying “It is freezing,” went straight along the street and turned off to the right towards the marketplace. When he reached the last house but one before the marketplace he stopped at the gate, pulled a whistle out of his pocket, and whistled with all his might as though giving a signal. He had not to wait more than a minute before a rosy-cheeked boy of about eleven, wearing a warm, neat and even stylish coat, darted out to meet him. This was Smurov, a boy in the preparatory class (two classes below Kolya Krassotkin), son of a well-to-do official. Apparently he was forbidden by his parents to associate with Krassotkin, who was well known to be a desperately naughty boy, so Smurov was obviously slipping out on the sly. He was—if the reader has not forgotten—one of the group of boys who two months before had thrown stones at Ilusha. He was the one who told Alyosha Karamazov about Ilusha.

cases.sentence: Ему пришлось ждать не более минуты, из калитки вдруг выскочил к нему ___, лет одиннадцати, тоже одетый в теплое, чистенькое и даже щегольское пальтецо.
cases.explain: «румяненький мальчик» — after the preposition «в», the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: — Я вас уже ___ жду, Красоткин, — с решительным видом проговорил Смуров, и мальчики зашагали к площади.
cases.explain: «целый час» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “I’ve been waiting for you for the last hour, Krassotkin,” said Smurov stolidly, and the boys strode towards the marketplace.

cases.sentence: — Я вас уже целый час жду, Красоткин, — с ___ проговорил Смуров, и мальчики зашагали к площади.
cases.explain: «решительным видом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “I’ve been waiting for you for the last hour, Krassotkin,” said Smurov stolidly, and the boys strode towards the marketplace.

cases.sentence: — Школьник, гнушайся лжи, это раз; даже для ___, два.
cases.explain: «доброго дела» — after the preposition «для», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Boy, shun a lie, that’s one thing; even with a good object—that’s another. Above all, I hope you’ve not told them anything about my coming.”

cases.sentence: «Ах, говорит, я говорил тебе, папа, что у меня ___, прежние, в них и прежде было неловко ходить».
cases.explain: «дурные сапожки» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Ah, he is bad, very bad! I believe he’s in consumption: he is quite conscious, but his breathing! His breathing’s gone wrong. The other day he asked to have his boots on to be led round the room. He tried to walk, but he couldn’t stand. ‘Ah, I told you before, father,’ he said, ‘that those boots were no good. I could never walk properly in them.’ He fancied it was his boots that made him stagger, but it was simply weakness, really. He won’t live another week. Herzenstube is looking after him. Now they are rich again—they’ve got heaps of money.”

cases.sentence: — ___, это мое дело, а не твое.
cases.explain: «Милый мальчик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “My dear boy, that’s my business, not yours. I am going of myself because I choose to, but you’ve all been hauled there by Alexey Karamazov—there’s a difference, you know. And how do you know? I may not be going to make it up at all. It’s a stupid expression.”

cases.sentence: Знаешь, он ___, и тогда вышла ошибка.
cases.explain: «благородный человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “It’s not Karamazov at all; it’s not his doing. Our fellows began going there of themselves. Of course, they went with Karamazov at first. And there’s been nothing of that sort—no silliness. First one went, and then another. His father was awfully pleased to see us. You know he will simply go out of his mind if Ilusha dies. He sees that Ilusha’s dying. And he seems so glad we’ve made it up with Ilusha. Ilusha asked after you, that was all. He just asks and says no more. His father will go out of his mind or hang himself. He behaved like a madman before. You know he is a very decent man. We made a mistake then. It’s all the fault of that murderer who beat him then.”

cases.sentence: Я мог бы и давно с ним познакомиться, но я в ___ люблю быть гордым.
cases.explain: «иных случаях» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Karamazov’s a riddle to me all the same. I might have made his acquaintance long ago, but I like to have a proper pride in some cases. Besides, I have a theory about him which I must work out and verify.”

cases.sentence: ___ торговали под своими навесами бубликами, нитками и проч.
cases.explain: «Городские бабы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Kolya subsided into dignified silence. Smurov, too, was silent. Smurov, of course, worshiped Krassotkin and never dreamed of putting himself on a level with him. Now he was tremendously interested at Kolya’s saying that he was “going of himself” to see Ilusha. He felt that there must be some mystery in Kolya’s suddenly taking it into his head to go to him that day. They crossed the marketplace, in which at that hour were many loaded wagons from the country and a great number of live fowls. The market women were selling rolls, cottons and threads, etc., in their booths. These Sunday markets were naively called “fairs” in the town, and there were many such fairs in the year. Perezvon ran about in the wildest spirits, sniffing about first one side, then the other. When he met other dogs they zealously smelt each other over according to the rules of canine etiquette.

cases.sentence: Такие ___ наивно называются у нас в городке ярмарками, и таких ярмарок бывает много в году.
cases.explain: «воскресные съезды» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: У людей все привычка, во всем, даже в государственных и в ___.
cases.explain: «политических отношениях» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Have you noticed, Smurov, that in the middle of winter we don’t feel so cold even when there are fifteen or eighteen degrees of frost as we do now, in the beginning of winter, when there is a sudden frost of twelve degrees, especially when there is not much snow. It’s because people are not used to it. Everything is habit with men, everything even in their social and political relations. Habit is the great motive-power. What a funny-looking peasant!”

cases.sentence: Привычка — ___.
cases.explain: «главный двигатель» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

It’s because people are not used to it. Everything is habit with men, everything even in their social and political relations. Habit is the great motive-power. What a funny-looking peasant!”

cases.sentence: Длинная ___ его вся заиндевела от мороза.
cases.explain: «русая борода» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Kolya pointed to a tall peasant, with a good-natured countenance in a long sheepskin coat, who was standing by his wagon, clapping together his hands, in their shapeless leather gloves, to warm them. His long fair beard was all white with frost.

cases.sentence: — Это ___, — заговорил Коля Смурову.
cases.explain: «хороший мужик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “That was a nice peasant,” Kolya observed to Smurov. “I like talking to the peasants, and am always glad to do them justice.”

cases.sentence: — Видишь, Смуров, не люблю я, когда переспрашивают, если не понимают с ___.
cases.explain: «первого слова» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “You know, Smurov, I don’t like being asked the same thing twice. I like people to understand at the first word. Some things can’t be explained. According to a peasant’s notions, schoolboys are whipped, and must be whipped. What would a schoolboy be if he were not whipped? And if I were to tell him we are not, he’d be disappointed. But you don’t understand that. One has to know how to talk to the peasants.”

cases.sentence: — Не беспокойся, ___ ничего не произойдет.
cases.explain: «нынешний раз» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Don’t be uneasy, nothing will happen this time. Hallo, Natasha!” he shouted to a market woman in one of the booths.

cases.sentence: — Какая я тебе Наташа, я Марья, — крикливо ответила торговка, далеко еще не ___.
cases.explain: «старая женщина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Call me Natasha! What next! My name is Marya,” the middle-aged market woman shouted at him.

cases.sentence: Он был в каком-то ___ и тотчас принялся грозить Коле кулаком.
cases.explain: «глупом волнении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: There was a roar of laughter among the other market women round her. Suddenly a man in a violent rage darted out from the arcade of shops close by. He was a young man, not a native of the town, with dark, curly hair and a long, pale face, marked with smallpox. He wore a long blue coat and a peaked cap, and looked like a merchant’s clerk. He was in a state of stupid excitement and brandished his fist at Kolya.

cases.sentence: — с ___, хотя все так же горячась, уставился на Колю парень.
cases.explain: «дурацким удивлением» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “What Trifon Nikititch?” asked the youth, staring with loutish amazement at Kolya, but still as angry as ever. Kolya scanned him gravely.

cases.sentence: — переговорила ___, — да какой он Трифон?
cases.explain: «другая баба» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “For the Kuzmitchovs?” repeated another woman. “But his name wasn’t Trifon. His name’s Kuzma, not Trifon; but the boy said Trifon Nikititch, so it can’t be the same.”

cases.sentence: — Это, вишь, не Трифон и не Сабанеев, это Чижов, — подхватила вдруг ___, доселе молчавшая и серьезно слушавшая, — Алексей Иванычем звать его.
cases.explain: «третья баба» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “His name is not Trifon and not Sabaneyev, it’s Tchizhov,” put in suddenly a third woman, who had hitherto been silent, listening gravely. “Alexey Ivanitch is his name. Tchizhov, Alexey Ivanitch.”

cases.sentence: А Коля шагал уже далеко с ___ в лице.
cases.explain: «победоносным выражением» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The woman guffawed. But Kolya was by now a long way off, marching along with a triumphant air. Smurov walked beside him, looking round at the shouting group far behind. He too was in high spirits, though he was still afraid of getting into some scrape in Kolya’s company.

cases.sentence: Дюжий мужик, медленно проходивший мимо и уже, должно быть, выпивший, с круглым ___ и с бородой с проседью, поднял голову и посмотрел на парнишку.
cases.explain: «простоватым лицом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: A sturdy-looking peasant, with a round, simple face and grizzled beard, who was walking by, raised his head and looked at the boy. He seemed not quite sober.

cases.sentence: Вдали на ___ пробило половину двенадцатого.
cases.explain: «соборных часах» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: In the distance the cathedral clock struck half-past eleven. The boys made haste and they walked as far as Captain Snegiryov’s lodging, a considerable distance, quickly and almost in silence. Twenty paces from the house Kolya stopped and told Smurov to go on ahead and ask Karamazov to come out to him.

cases.sentence: Мальчики заспешили и остальной довольно еще ___ до жилища штабс-капитана Снегирева прошли быстро и почти уже не разговаривая.
cases.explain: «длинный путь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
